context: Six-panel scatterplot matrix of synthetic health metrics (height, weight, age, cholesterol, BP, VO2 max, resting HR) for 300 points across three activity groups, with composable brush selections (union/intersection) and progressive annotations (centroid crosshair, outlier flags).
first_impression: Clean, honest scatter matrix with data-driven scales and no baseline violations — the right chart type for the encoding.
what_works: Scales use d3.extent(data).nice() for all axes, so domains are fully data-driven and robust to the synthetic dataset; circle radius encodes only selection state (3.5/4/2.5 px), not data magnitude, so there is no lie factor.
what_doesnt: No key function in .data(data) joins — benign here since data is static, but would cause visual corruption if data order changed after initial render; outlier z-score threshold (2.2) is arbitrary and undocumented, risking inconsistent flagging across different data distributions.
